q: Ana taps Pay. The server charges her card, but the answer is lost, and her app times out after 10 seconds. What does the timeout tell the app?
options: The charge failed, so it is safe to send again with no guard
The charge worked, so the app should stop
Nothing about the result: it means "I do not know", so the retry must be harmless
The server is broken and must be restarted
why: A timeout only says the answer did not arrive. The card may or may not have been charged. Without a guard, a retry charges twice. So the app gives the action a name once, and the server answers a repeat with "I already did that".

q: Which of these is safe to repeat (twice leaves the same result as once)?
options: Add 10 to the balance
Create a payment with POST
Set the balance to 50
Add an item to the end of a list
why: Setting a value to 50 twice leaves 50. Adding 10 twice adds 20, and a second POST makes a second payment. GET, PUT and DELETE are safe to repeat. POST and PATCH are not, unless you add a request key.

q: Two copies of the same request with key k-42 reach two servers at the same moment. The code does: find the key, and if it is not there, charge and save. What happens, and what is the fix?
options: Both find nothing and both charge. Insert the key first as "in progress" and let the table's unique rule pick one winner
Only one finds nothing, because the database makes reads take turns
Both are refused, which is safe, so no fix is needed
Both charge, but the card provider removes one. No fix is needed
why: This is the check-then-save race again: both read "not there" before either writes. If you insert first, Postgres lets one insert win. The other gets 0 rows, sees a row "in progress", and answers 409. The app asks again later and gets the saved answer.

q: A bug sends the key k-41 again, but with the amount 200,000 instead of the first request's 100,000. What should the server do?
options: Charge 200,000, because the client knows best
Send back the saved answer for 100,000, as if nothing changed
Delete the key and start over
Answer 422 and do nothing, because the body check does not match the first request
why: The server keeps a short code of the first request's body. Same body and done: send the saved answer. Same body and still running: 409. Different body: 422. A key names one action, so it cannot be reused for another.

q: A retry loop makes a new random key inside the loop on each try. The first two tries time out, and the third works. What did the server see?
options: One payment, because the amount is the same
Nothing, because the keys were not sent
One payment, because the server compares the bodies
Up to three payments, because each try had a different key and looked like a new action
why: The key names the action, not the try. Make it once, before the first try, and send the same key every time. Then all tries are one action, and a repeat gets the saved answer.

q: A client gets these answers: (a) a 503, (b) a 400, (c) a 429 with Retry-After. Which should it retry, assuming the request is safe to repeat?
options: All three, because any error might pass
(a) now with backoff, and (c) after waiting. Not (b), because the same request fails the same way every time
Only (b), because a client error is the easiest to fix
None of them, because a retry only makes it worse
why: Retry timeouts and 5xx, and wait for 409 and 429. Never retry other 4xx, because the request itself is wrong. Retry 2 or 3 times, and wait a bit longer each time with a little randomness, so many apps do not all retry in the same second.
